questions.q:
In the lab's table-level ACL below, what two conditions allow a user to open an employee record?
```javascript
answer = gs.hasRole('hr_user') || current.manager == gs.getUserID();
```
options: Holding the hr_user role, or being the manager listed on that specific employee record
Holding the hr_user role, or being a member of the hr_compensation group
Only holding the hr_compensation_admin role
Only being the employee whose record it is
questions.explain: The script is an OR of two conditions: the hr_user role, or current.manager matching the logged-in user's sys_id.

questions.q: A user holds `hr_user` but is not a member of the `hr_compensation` group and does not hold `hr_compensation_admin`. Using the lab's two ACLs, what do they see on the employee record?
options: The entire record, including salary_band, because passing the table-level ACL grants every field automatically
Nothing at all -- the record fails to open
The record, with salary_band absent or blank, because the field-level ACL evaluates separately and fails
An error, because two ACLs can never apply to the same record
questions.explain: Table-level and field-level ACLs are independent checks that both must pass. Passing one never substitutes for the other.

questions.q: Why does the field-level script use `gs.getUser().isMemberOf('c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8')` instead of a `GlideRecord` query against `sys_user_grmember`?
options: GlideRecord queries are not permitted inside ACL scripts at all
isMemberOf() reuses GlideUser's already-cached membership data instead of issuing a fresh query on every access, which matters because this field is read constantly across list views and reports
There is no real performance difference between the two approaches
isMemberOf() checks roles, not group membership, so it answers a different question
questions.explain: This is the Lesson 5 guidance applied to a real field: avoid a per-access database query when a cached check already answers the same question.

questions.q: A user holds `hr_compensation_admin` but does not hold `hr_user` and is not that employee's manager. What happens when they try to view the record?
options: They see salary_band but nothing else on the record
They fail the table-level ACL and cannot open the record at all, so the field-level ACL is never reached
They see the full record including salary_band, since hr_compensation_admin overrides every other ACL
The field-level ACL runs first and grants them access to the whole record
questions.explain: The table-level ACL is evaluated for the record as a whole. Failing it blocks access before any field-level check is relevant.

questions.q: Why does this lab's field-level ACL design "hold up under load," as the lesson puts it, across a list view showing hundreds of employee records?
options: Because list views skip ACL evaluation entirely
Because isMemberOf() avoids issuing a separate database query per row, unlike a manual GlideRecord lookup would
Because salary_band is cached in the browser after the first page load
Because table-level ACLs replace the need for field-level ACLs in list views
questions.explain: The same reasoning from Lesson 5 applies at scale: a cached membership check doesn't multiply query cost per row the way a manual query would.
